findings.title: Nonabelian transversal exception incorrectly normalizes columns on the left
findings.check: For every rank r>=3, H=<12>xC2^(r-1) in S3xC2^(r-1), b=(123), A=H-{e,a}, B=Ab. Quotient-symbol sum precludes a transversal; difference subgroups H and b^-1Hb are distinct, ruling out both printed exceptions.
findings.counterevidence: Proof uses correct right column normalization; abelian specialization unaffected.
findings.impact: Advertised nonabelian classification false for unbounded sizes; Theorem 1.1 not refuted.
findings.repair: Use B g2 in second exception. Covariance and missing-family repair verified; full corrected classification not independently proved.

findings.title: Division-path and orthomorphism guarantees allow unavailable identity colour
findings.check: All odd N>=5: G=Z_N, x=0,y=-1,V=G-{0,-1},C=G-{1}. Every stated division hypothesis holds; zero is in C but on no edge, so N-1 rainbow edges cannot use only N-2 available colours. Separate asymptotic construction meets the random perturbation and sum hypotheses in 4.9.
findings.counterevidence: Multiplication case differs; actual sequenceability applications remove identity.
findings.impact: Printed division-path guarantee and random orthomorphism statement false; large-group sequenceability not refuted.
findings.repair: Exclude identity for division/orthomorphism cases in all groups; necessity verified, entire corrected sufficiency proof pending.

findings.title: Lemma 3.9 permits deterministic leftovers too large for the random reservoir
findings.check: C2^m with index-two cosets H,J; p=.1,q=.45; X=(H\R_A,H\R_B,J\R_C). Every edge uses R, leaving at least (.75+o(1))n vertices, larger than n^.9999 asymptotically.
findings.counterevidence: Actual main application has q <= reservoir density /100.
findings.impact: False extra auxiliary range; no failure of actual small-leftover use established.
findings.repair: q<=p/5 makes q,q,p-2q partition feasible; full quantitative replacement not certified.

findings.title: Lemma 3.4 lacks a density bound
findings.check: r disjoint C2 multiplication blocks are linear, degree 2, with n=2r vertices per part and delta=2/n; at most r matching edges leave 3n/2 vertices.
findings.counterevidence: An arbitrary density-dependent size threshold for fixed positive delta avoids this family but supplies no uniform polynomial-density bound; actual use has polynomially growing degree.
findings.impact: Unrestricted auxiliary scope false; main random theorem not refuted.
findings.repair: No full corrected theorem asserted; explicit density/error conditions and edge-to-vertex count required.

findings.title: Core preprocessing requires covering vertices excluded from its host
findings.check: p=1/4, sufficiently large n, S=U={v}, v nonidentity, satisfies all hypotheses but cannot be covered in H_G[Q]\U. Also S outside Q with U empty. Main use includes target vertices outside R superset Q.
findings.counterevidence: Intended local statement is repairable; core theorem not refuted.
findings.impact: Invalid stated lemma and core invocation, even though repair is local.
findings.repair: Require S intersect U empty and matching in H_G[S union Q]\U with exactly one S vertex per edge and all remaining vertices Q\(S union U). Inverse-orbit matching extraction plus Chernoff and greedy proof given; main invocation fits.

unresolved_claims: Full corrected application and dense-matching sufficiency not independently established

focused_scientific_check.scope: Independent focused checks of existing reported Problems only; no full initial review, unrelated issue search, new author-code execution or new compilation.
focused_scientific_check.computation_reuse: Existing reviewer-created scripts and outputs were read and reused with current byte hashes. The native helper independently checked the analytic arguments and did not rerun these scripts.

checks.reason: The nonabelian family A=H-{e,a}, B=Ab has no transversal by the elementary-abelian sum invariant. A^-1A=H and B^-1B=b^-1Hb differ, excluding the common-left-normalized exception, while the coset exception fails by cardinality. This is an unbounded counterexample to the advertised classification; right column normalization repairs the missing family but a full corrected theorem is not certified.

Division edges exclude equal endpoints in the source, so colour e is absent for every group. Odd cyclic N with x=0,y=-1,V=G-{0,-1},C=G-{1} meets cardinality, endpoint and sum hypotheses. The disjoint-random-set example has a valid uniform bounded-differences estimate for all shifts; O(sqrt(N)log(N)) edits eventually fit the stated fixed-p tolerance. Multiplication and identity-free sequenceability applications remain outside the refutation.

The source really states q<=5p, confirmed on PDF17 image. At p=1/10,q=9/20 the two subgroup parts and one opposite-coset part forbid every all-X edge, giving (.75+o(1))n uncovered vertices. The sublinear contradiction is asymptotic, not the stored n=65536 illustration. The actual Theorem5.33 reservoir density is (1-10^-5)p and the small leftover fits its /100 bound, so central damage from the excessive range is not shown.

The four edges of the C2 block are pairwise intersecting, linear and degree two. r disjoint blocks with n=2r and delta=2/n leave 3n/2 vertices; all regularity hypotheses hold. The source expressly calls for polynomially varying parameters, supporting the report uniform-scope reading. Arbitrary fixed-delta thresholds and the dense actual use are explicitly distinguished.

Both S=U={v} and S outside Q with U empty satisfy the printed lemma and cannot be saturated in its stated host. The main invocation explicitly uses wanted vertices outside R, proving the core dependency. For the local replacement, inverse-orbit candidate multigraph degree<=4 gives at least n/50 disjoint orbit pairs, independent p^2 events and a uniform p^2n/100 reservoir. At most5t forbidden vertices and linearity justify greedy coverage; S intersect U empty and Q minus U in the target hold in the application.
